name: The Nab II
summary: 411 of 443 raw chips required. Dirt-covered chips are collectible after revealing them; the cloner-tile partition and key sequence need a constructive route.
limitations: No winning replay and no universal impossibility proof established. Data counts or unsuccessful play are not treated as impossibility.

experiments.result: Decoded both 1024-cell DAT planes and exact level metadata; initialized production MS runtime and rendered actual game sprites.
A run confined to the upper region collected 213 of the required 411 chips and acquired the buried red key, then became cornered near (24,18). No complete solution or impossibility follows.
